name: Coffee drinking among the Sufis of Yemen
summary: Sufis in Yemen were drinking coffee during their night vigils by the fifteenth century, and from Yemen the drink spread across the east and eventually to the Americas.
description: Coffee, a drink steeped from the dried, roasted and ground berries of the coffee tree, probably originated in Ethiopia and was introduced to Yemen in the fourteenth or fifteenth century. A sixteenth-century writer, Jaziri, credits the Aden jurist Dhabhani, who died in 1470 and had met the drink in Africa, with introducing it to Sufi circles, where it was drunk during night vigils; another report of his credits a Shadhili shaikh at Mocha who died in 1418. From Yemen it spread through the east and eventually to Latin America.

impact.note: All later coffee drinking descends from Yemen and reached many societies on several continents, but no source here shows most of humanity drinks it, so reach is 2, lowered from 3; a new daily stimulant drink (depth 1); the coffeehouse and the coffee trade followed (generativity 1).

date.label: by 1470
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: A later report credits Dhabhani, a jurist from Aden who died in 1470, with introducing coffee to Sufi circles, where it was drunk during night vigils for prayer.

evidence.supports: Ḏabḥānī (d. 875/1470), a jurist from Aden, had become ac­quainted with it during a period of exile in Africa and had observed its medicinal effects, subsequently introducing it in Sufi circles, where it was drunk during night vigils for prayer

events.statement: The coffee drink, which probably originated in Ethiopia, was introduced to Yemen in the fourteenth or fifteenth century.

evidence.supports: The beverage probably originated in Ethiopia and was introduced in the 14th or 15th century to Yemen, whence it spread throughout the east and eventually to Latin America

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Primary Arabic sources for Yemeni coffee drinking, above all Jaziri (c. 1558) as discussed by Hattox (1985), were not opened; the record rests on an encyclopaedia summary.
Which of Jaziri's two reports is right: Dhabhani of Aden (died 1470) or the Shadhili shaikh at Mocha (died 1418).
Whether coffee was roasted and brewed in Ethiopia before it reached Yemen; if a dated Ethiopian record is found it becomes the first known.
The tenth-century medical references (Razi, Ibn Sina) to bunn and whether they describe the drink.
A more exact place than the country: Aden or Mocha, once a primary source is read.

research.note: The Encyclopaedia Iranica says the beverage probably originated in Ethiopia and was introduced to Yemen, and reports a sixteenth-century account that Dhabhani met it in Africa. No dated Ethiopian record of the drink is cited, so Yemen remains the earliest documented coffee drinking.
